title: Visual scope definition - building-only tile claim boundary

defect_summary.overclaim: The tile FBX generation pipeline was implicitly described as producing a 'complete visual map' or 'CARLA Large Map' visual product. In reality, the tile FBX pipeline ONLY produces building/clutter FBX files (from OSM2World -> Blender). Road/junction/sidewalk/marking visuals are owned by CARLA/OpenDRIVE import, not by the FBX pipeline.
defect_summary.misleading_docs: Documentation and claim boundaries implied the FBX tiles constituted a complete visual map, when they only cover buildings/clutter.

corrected_semantics.tile_scope: BUILDING_OCCUPIED_CELLS_ONLY - The tile FBX artifacts ONLY cover building/clutter geometry in occupied grid cells. They do NOT include: road surfaces, junctions, sidewalks, road markings, traffic lights, or any road-adjacent visual elements.
corrected_semantics.proves_complete_visual_map: false - Explicitly documented in tile_fbx_generator.py manifest claim_boundary and in TileFbxResult.claim_boundary.

visual_pipeline_architecture.master_visual_frozen: Deterministic spatial partition combining all three

tests.updated_claim_boundary: TileFbxResult.claim_boundary now explicitly states: 'Offline FBX generation only. This tile has NOT been imported by UE4/UE5 Editor or cooked; runtime streaming/seam behavior is UNCONFIRMED until the live UE4 track runs.'

regression_results.focused: Tile FBX generator tests pass (28 passed)

residual_risks: Downstream consumers (e.g., UE4 cooking scripts) may still assume tile FBXs provide complete visual coverage. Explicit documentation and claim_boundary updates are necessary but not sufficient; consumer code must be audited.
The master visual scene architecture (OC-46 item 15) is a future integration point, not yet implemented. This scope definition prepares for it but does not implement it.
OSM2World configuration (excludeWorldModule) explicitly excludes roads/rail/aeroway/parking - this is correct for the claimed scope but must be documented to avoid confusion.
